{{short description|Riemannian n-manifold embeds locally in an (n + 1)-manifold with flat Ricci curvature}}
{{about|the embedding of Riemannian manifolds||Campbell's theorem (probability)}}

'''Campbell's theorem''', named after [[John Edward Campbell]], also known as '''Campbell’s embedding theorem''' and the '''Campbell-Magaard theorem''', is a [[mathematical theorem]] guaranteeing that any n-dimensional [[Riemannian manifold]] can be locally embedded in an (''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)-dimensional Ricci-flat Riemannian manifold.<ref>Romero, Carlos, Reza Tavakol, and Roustam Zalaltedinov. ''The Embedding of General Relativity in Five Dimensions''. N.p.: Springer Netherlands, 2005.</ref>

==Statement==
Campbell's theorem states that any [[n-dimensional|''n''-dimensional]] [[Riemannian manifold]] can be [[embedding|embedded]] locally in an (''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)-manifold with a [[Ricci curvature]] of ''R''<sub>'''a''&nbsp;''b''</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0. The theorem also states, in similar form, that an ''n''-dimensional [[pseudo-Riemannian manifold]] can be both locally and isometrically embedded in an ''n''(''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)/2-[[pseudo-Euclidean space]].

==Applications==
Campbell’s theorem can be used to produce the embedding of numerous [[Spacetime symmetries|4-dimensional spacetimes]] in [[five-dimensional space|5-dimensional]] [[Ricci-flat manifold|Ricci-flat spaces]]. It is also used to embed a class of [[n-dimensional space|''n''-dimensional Einstein spaces]].<ref>Lindsey, James E., et al. "On Applications of Campbell's Embedding Theorem." On Applications of Campbell's Embedding Theorem 14 (1997): 1&nbsp;17. Abstract.</ref>
